transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been troubling you or what brings you in today?

I… I guess what finally scared me enough to come in is that I keep thinking it would be easier if I just didn’t wake up. And then sometimes, driving home from the clinic — we have this one stretch of road that’s kind of dark, and I’m usually replaying the whole day, the animals, the owners, all of it — I catch myself wondering what would happen if I just… didn’t turn the wheel.
How often have you been having these thoughts about not waking up or not turning the wheel, and do they come and go or feel constant?

It’s… it’s been happening enough that it doesn’t feel like a one-off anymore. The “not waking up” thought kind of pops up a lot, like when I’m exhausted and I get into bed and the house is finally quiet. And the driving thing— that’s not every single time, but there’s this stretch after the clinic, and if it’s dark and I’m already replaying everything from the day, I’ll suddenly think, what if I just didn’t turn the wheel?

It comes and goes, I guess, but lately it’s been coming back more than I’m comfortable with.
Have you ever done anything, even small things, to try to make those thoughts come true, or have you actively avoided acting on them?

I haven’t… I don’t think I’ve actually done anything to make it happen. It’s more that the thought shows up and scares me. Like the driving thing — I’ll be on that dark stretch after the clinic, and my brain just sort of says, what if you didn’t turn the wheel? And then I grip the wheel tighter or try to focus on the road signs, anything really.

And the not waking up thing… that’s more when I’m in bed and exhausted, and it feels like it would be simpler not to have to do the next day. But I haven’t taken steps, no. I think coming here was me trying not to let it get to that point.
Have you noticed that you’re not enjoying things the way you used to, or that even activities you once looked forward to now feel like a chore?

Yeah… yes, definitely. I used to have these little things that sort of made me feel like me, if that makes sense. My camera, for one—I used to take it out even just around the yard, or on walks, noticing light and birds and silly things like frost on a fence post.

And the bird feeders… I still see them, obviously, they’re right there, but I don’t really check them with any real interest anymore. Same with the garden. Normally I’d be thinking ahead, what’s coming up, what needs moving or planting, but now I just… don’t care. It all feels like one more thing sitting there.

It’s frightening, actually, because those things weren’t just hobbies. They were how I kind of knew I was still myself.
Have you noticed that most days, you feel down or hopeless, even when there’s nothing specific going wrong?

Most days, yes. It’s like the color has drained out of everything, even if nothing dramatic has happened that day.

The house can be busy around me—people moving around, normal noises, laundry going, dishes, all of that—and I’ll still feel this hopelessness sitting there. Sometimes I end up in the laundry room crying because I just can’t stand anyone seeing me like that. It feels ridiculous to hide behind a basket of towels, but… that’s where I go.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight lately—like eating much less or more than usual, or losing or gaining weight without trying?

Yeah… I think so. It’s been sort of all over the place, but lately I mostly just… pick at things. Like toast, or I’ll have coffee and tell myself I’ll eat properly later.

Then I’ll get to the end of a clinic shift and realize I’ve barely eaten all day. Which is stupid, because at work we’re always fussing over animals not eating, watching every little sign, and meanwhile I’m standing there running on coffee like that somehow doesn’t count. I don’t know about the weight exactly—I haven’t been keeping track—but the eating has definitely been off.
Have you noticed that you're moving more slowly than usual, or that you can't sit still and feel restless?

I don’t know if I’d say moving slowly exactly… there have been times it’s almost the opposite, like I can’t leave things alone.

I started taking extra shifts at the clinic, and then at home I redid the whole care schedule for the house—who was doing what, when, like feeding, errands, all of it. I even started contacting contractors about things that didn’t need to be tackled right then. I had this whole system in my head like I was coordinating some huge hospital project, you know, with everyone’s tasks lined up… except no one had asked me to take all that on.

And then of course people don’t follow the plan because they didn’t even know they were in the plan, and I’d get frustrated, which sounds ridiculous saying it out loud. But yes, restless maybe. Like I had to keep organizing and pushing things forward.
Have you noticed a loss of energy or feeling fatigued, even when you haven’t been doing much physically?

Yes. That’s actually been one of the harder parts to ignore.

At work, even just walking from the treatment area over to the lab benches can feel like I’m dragging myself through mud. And it’s not like that’s far—I mean, I’ve done that walk a thousand times, usually with samples in one hand and someone calling from the other room about a dog that won’t cooperate or a cat that’s decided to become a chainsaw with fur.

But lately it feels absurdly heavy. Like my body is just… resisting.

And then by the time I get home, I’m wiped out. I can barely get dinner together or help with the evening care routine. I’ll stand in the kitchen and look at what needs doing, and it feels like it might as well be a mountain.
How long have these feelings been going on now—like the hopelessness, the loss of interest, the fatigue and the thoughts about not waking up?

Um… I think it’s been hanging over me for about eleven months now. Not every single day has looked exactly the same, I guess, and I kept telling myself it was just stress or work or… you know, life being life.

But looking back, it’s been there most of this time. And this past month especially, it’s like someone turned the weight of it up. That’s when it started feeling unbearable.
Have you ever experienced a period like this before, or is this the first time you've felt this way for an extended period?

I’m not sure I can give you a clean yes or no on that. I mean, I’ve had rough stretches before—who hasn’t, right? Especially working in a clinic, it’s like everything piles up, and then you come home and there’s still laundry and appointments and someone needs something, and you just sort of keep moving.

But as far as feeling this way for this long… I don’t know. I’m trying to think back, and my memory kind of turns into a junk drawer. There were periods where I was definitely not myself, but whether it was like this, or for this length of time… I can’t really say.
Have you ever had a period in the past where you felt down or lost interest in things for more than two months at a time?

I… honestly don’t know. More than two months is hard for me to pin down.

I can remember being “off” before, like just not wanting to do much or feeling kind of low, but then I start second-guessing whether it was really that long or if I’m just blending things together. Time gets weird when you’re busy, you know? At the clinic, whole seasons can pass and I’m still thinking it’s the same month because it’s just appointments, lab work, cleaning cages, repeat.

So… maybe? But I can’t say for sure that there was a clear stretch longer than two months like you’re asking.
Can you think back to any specific time in the past when you felt down or lost interest in things for more than two months straight, even if it wasn’t recent?

I’m trying to, I really am… but no specific time is coming up clearly enough that I could point to it and say, “Yes, that was more than two months straight.”

There were times I remember feeling kind of flattened out, I guess, but then I get stuck on whether it was actually that long or if I’m just remembering the general mess of life at the time. Like, some years at work blur together—especially when we were short-staffed, and there’d be these weeks where every day felt like the same day, and then suddenly it was fall or winter or whatever.

So… I don’t know. I can’t honestly give you a specific past stretch like that.
Can you recall any time in your life, even if it wasn't recent, when you felt down or lost interest in things for a period of two months or more without a clear break?

Yeah… I think if I’m being honest, this current stretch probably counts. It’s been hanging over me for, I don’t know, maybe around eleven months now. Not always at the exact same volume, if that makes sense—like sometimes it was background noise and I could still get through work and errands and all of that—but it was still there.

And then this past month, it’s gotten… unbearable, really. But it didn’t come out of nowhere. It’s more like it had already been sitting on me for most of the year, and then recently it just got heavier.
